description: Data Interpretation question bank derived from Mental Ability - Data Interpretation comprehensive notes. Covers Fundamentals, Tables, Graphs & Charts, Percentages & Proportions, Ratios & Proportions, Averages/Totals/Comparative Measures, Comparative Data, Question Types, Solved Sets, and Formulas. Verify before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is Data Interpretation (DI)?

options.A: The process of collecting raw data from the field
options.B: The process of reading, organising, analysing, comparing, and drawing conclusions from numerical or categorical information presented in tables, graphs, and charts
options.C: The process of storing data in a computer
options.D: The process of deleting unnecessary data

questions.explanation: Data Interpretation is the analysis of information presented in a structured form to answer questions, identify patterns, calculate values, and make comparisons.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is data?

options.A: A collection of facts, figures, observations, or measurements gathered for reference or analysis
options.B: Only numerical values stored in a table
options.C: A graph drawn on paper
options.D: The conclusion drawn from a chart

questions.explanation: Data is a collection of facts, figures, observations, or measurements gathered for reference or analysis.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is raw data?

options.A: Data already summarised in a pie chart
options.B: Information in its original, unprocessed form before classification, summarisation, or analysis
options.C: Data that has been averaged

questions.explanation: Raw data is information in its original, unprocessed form before classification, summarisation, or analysis.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is structured data?

options.A: Data organised according to a defined format, such as rows and columns in a table
options.B: Any data written in a paragraph
options.C: Data without any units

questions.explanation: Structured data is organised according to a defined format, such as rows and columns in a table.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a data set?

options.A: A single number
options.B: A collection of related observations or values used for analysis
options.C: A type of graph

questions.explanation: A data set is a collection of related observations or values used for analysis.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a variable in data interpretation?

options.A: A fixed constant that never changes
options.B: A characteristic that can take different values, such as year, population, income, production, or number of candidates
options.C: A type of pie chart

questions.explanation: A variable is a characteristic that can take different values, such as year, population, income, production, or number of candidates.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is frequency?

options.A: The number of times a particular value or category occurs
options.B: The average of all values
options.C: The difference between the largest and smallest value
options.D: The unit of a data set

questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of times a particular value or category occurs.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does a unit of measurement specify?

options.A: The colour of a chart
options.B: What a number represents, such as rupees, persons, kilograms, tonnes, kilometres, or percentage
options.C: The title of a graph
options.D: The number of rows in a table

questions.explanation: A unit specifies what a number represents, such as rupees, persons, kilograms, tonnes, kilometres, or percentage.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Why must the title and unit be checked before solving a DI question?

options.A: Because the title identifies the subject and scope of the data, while the unit tells how to interpret the figures; ignoring units can produce a numerically correct but contextually wrong answer
options.B: Because titles are always printed in bold
options.C: Because units are optional in exams
options.D: Because checking them saves time only

questions.explanation: The title identifies the subject and scope of the data, while the unit tells how to interpret the figures. Ignoring units can produce a numerically correct but contextually wrong answer.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is an absolute value in a data set?

options.A: A percentage or ratio
options.B: The actual reported quantity, such as 450 students or 8 lakh
options.C: The average of a data set
options.D: A value that is always negative

questions.explanation: An absolute value is the actual reported quantity, such as 450 students or 8 lakh.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a relative value?

options.A: The actual reported quantity
options.B: A value that expresses one quantity in relation to another, such as a percentage, ratio, or proportion
options.C: The largest value in a table

questions.explanation: A relative value expresses one quantity in relation to another, such as a percentage, ratio, or proportion.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a trend in data?

options.A: A single outlier
options.B: The general direction in which data changes over time, such as increasing, decreasing, or remaining broadly stable
options.C: The title of a table

questions.explanation: A trend is the general direction in which data changes over time, such as increasing, decreasing, or remaining broadly stable.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is an outlier?

options.A: The most frequent value
options.B: A value that is unusually far from the other observations in a data set
options.C: The average of all values
options.D: The middle value of a data set

questions.explanation: An outlier is a value that is unusually far from the other observations in a data set.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is an estimate?

options.A: An exact value calculated to two decimal places
options.B: An approximate value obtained by rounding or using a reasonable calculation when an exact value is unnecessary
options.C: A value that is always wrong
options.D: The maximum value in a data set

questions.explanation: An estimate is an approximate value obtained by rounding or using a reasonable calculation when an exact value is unnecessary.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a data table?

options.A: A visual display using bars
options.B: A structure that organises information into rows and columns so that values can be located and compared systematically
options.C: A circle divided into sectors
options.D: A list of unorganised raw data

questions.explanation: A data table organises information into rows and columns so that values can be located and compared systematically.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does a row usually represent in a table?

options.A: A variable or measurement
options.B: One item, category, location, group, or time period, depending on the table design
options.C: The title of the table

questions.explanation: A row usually represents one item, category, location, group, or time period, depending on the table design.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does a column usually represent in a table?

options.A: One category or time period
options.B: A variable or measurement, such as year, sales, expenditure, profit, or population
options.C: The total of a row

questions.explanation: A column usually represents a variable or measurement, such as year, sales, expenditure, profit, or population.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a simple table?

options.A: A table that presents one or a small number of variables for different categories or periods
options.B: A table with more than ten columns
options.C: A table that classifies data by two variables
options.D: A table drawn as a circle

questions.explanation: A simple table presents one or a small number of variables for different categories or periods.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a two-way table?

options.A: A table with only one row
options.B: A table that classifies data according to two variables, such as gender and department or region and product
options.C: A table with two titles
options.D: A table that cannot be totalled

questions.explanation: A two-way table classifies data according to two variables, such as gender and department or region and product.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a multiple or complex table?

options.A: A table with only percentages
options.B: A table that presents several variables or categories and may require combining values from different rows and columns
options.C: A table with a single value

questions.explanation: A multiple or complex table presents several variables or categories and may require combining values from different rows and columns.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How should a table-based DI question be approached?

options.A: Read the title, identify row and column headings, note the units, locate the required cells, and then perform only the calculation asked
options.B: Calculate every possible value first
options.C: Ignore the headings and read numbers randomly
options.D: Convert all values to percentages first

questions.explanation: Read the title, identify row and column headings, note the units, locate the required cells, and then perform only the calculation asked.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is a row total calculated?

options.A: By adding all relevant values across that row
options.B: By adding all values down a column
options.C: By multiplying the first and last value in the row

questions.explanation: A row total is calculated by adding all relevant values across that row.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is a column total calculated?

options.A: By adding all relevant values down that column
options.B: By adding all values across a row
options.C: By dividing the column by the number of rows
options.D: By subtracting the smallest from the largest

questions.explanation: A column total is calculated by adding all relevant values down that column.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is a grand total calculated?

options.A: By adding only the first row and first column
options.B: By adding all category totals, ensuring that no value is counted twice
options.C: By averaging all row totals

questions.explanation: A grand total is calculated by adding all category totals, ensuring that no value is counted twice.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is an average from a table calculated?

options.A: Sum of the relevant values ÷ Number of values
options.B: Largest value − Smallest value
options.C: Sum of values × Number of values
options.D: Number of values ÷ Sum of values

questions.explanation: Average = Sum of the relevant values ÷ Number of values.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a common table-reading error?

options.A: Using a calculator
options.B: Reading the correct number from the wrong row, column, year, or unit
options.C: Reading the title of the table

questions.explanation: Reading the correct number from the wrong row, column, year, or unit is a common error. Trace both the row heading and column heading before using a figure.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a graph?

options.A: A visual representation of data that helps show patterns, relationships, changes, or comparisons
options.B: A table of raw numbers
options.C: A written paragraph describing data

questions.explanation: A graph is a visual representation of data that helps show patterns, relationships, changes, or comparisons.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a chart?

options.A: A visual display of information, often using bars, lines, sectors, symbols, or pictures
options.B: A collection of raw data
options.C: A unit of measurement

questions.explanation: A chart is a visual display of information, often using bars, lines, sectors, symbols, or pictures.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a bar graph?

options.A: A circle divided into sectors
options.B: A graph that uses rectangular bars to compare values across separate categories, where bar lengths or heights are proportional to the values
options.C: A graph that connects data points with a line

questions.explanation: A bar graph uses rectangular bars to compare values across separate categories. Bar lengths or heights are proportional to the values.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a horizontal bar graph?

options.A: It displays categories along the vertical axis and values along the horizontal axis
options.B: It displays categories along the horizontal axis and values along the vertical axis
options.C: It uses sectors instead of bars

questions.explanation: A horizontal bar graph displays categories along the vertical axis and values along the horizontal axis.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a vertical bar graph or column chart?

options.A: It displays categories along the vertical axis and values along the horizontal axis
options.B: It displays categories along the horizontal axis and values along the vertical axis
options.C: It connects data points with lines

questions.explanation: A vertical bar graph or column chart displays categories along the horizontal axis and values along the vertical axis.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a double bar graph?

options.A: A graph with two axes only
options.B: A graph that uses two bars for each category to compare two related data series, such as male and female enrolment across years
options.C: A graph with two titles

questions.explanation: A double bar graph uses two bars for each category to compare two related data series, such as male and female enrolment across years.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a multiple bar graph?

options.A: A graph that uses more than two bars for each category to compare several related series
options.B: A graph with only one bar per category
options.C: A graph that uses sectors

questions.explanation: A multiple bar graph uses more than two bars for each category to compare several related series.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a line graph?

options.A: A graph that uses rectangular bars
options.B: A graph that connects plotted data points and is particularly useful for showing changes or trends over time
options.C: A circle divided into sectors

questions.explanation: A line graph connects plotted data points and is particularly useful for showing changes or trends over time.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a pie chart?

options.A: A graph that uses bars of different heights
options.B: A circle divided into sectors, with each sector representing a proportion of the total
options.C: A graph that connects data points with a line
options.D: A graph using symbols or pictures

questions.explanation: A pie chart is a circle divided into sectors, with each sector representing a proportion of the total.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a histogram?

options.A: A circle divided into sectors
options.B: A graph that displays the frequency distribution of continuous numerical data using adjoining rectangles for class intervals
options.C: A graph that uses pictures to represent quantities

questions.explanation: A histogram displays the frequency distribution of continuous numerical data using adjoining rectangles for class intervals.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between a bar graph and a histogram?

options.A: A bar graph usually compares separate categories and has gaps between bars; a histogram represents continuous class intervals and normally has adjoining bars
options.B: A bar graph is always circular; a histogram is always triangular
options.C: A bar graph has no axes; a histogram has axes
options.D: A bar graph uses percentages only; a histogram uses ratios only

questions.explanation: A bar graph usually compares separate categories and has gaps between bars; a histogram represents continuous class intervals and normally has adjoining bars.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a pictograph?

options.A: A graph that uses pictures or symbols to represent quantities, where each symbol has a specified value or key
options.B: A graph that connects data points
options.C: A circle divided into sectors
options.D: A graph of continuous class intervals

questions.explanation: A pictograph uses pictures or symbols to represent quantities. Each symbol has a specified value or key.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a scatter plot?

options.A: A graph that displays paired numerical observations as points to show the relationship or association between two variables
options.B: A graph that uses rectangular bars
options.C: A circle divided into sectors

questions.explanation: A scatter plot displays paired numerical observations as points to show the relationship or association between two variables.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a stacked bar chart?

options.A: A chart that divides each bar into segments to show both the total and its component parts
options.B: A chart with only one segment per bar
options.C: A chart that uses a line only

questions.explanation: A stacked bar chart divides each bar into segments to show both the total and its component parts.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a 100% stacked bar chart?

options.A: It displays each bar as 100% with segments showing the percentage composition of each category
options.B: It displays only totals without components
options.C: It displays a single bar only
options.D: It displays values on a logarithmic scale

questions.explanation: A 100% stacked bar chart displays each bar as 100% with segments showing the percentage composition of each category.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a combo chart?

options.A: A chart that uses two chart types, such as bars and a line, to display related data series together
options.B: A chart with two titles
options.C: A chart with only one data series

questions.explanation: A combination chart uses two chart types, such as bars and a line, to display related data series together.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the horizontal axis of a graph called?

options.A: Y-axis
options.B: X-axis
options.C: Z-axis

questions.explanation: The horizontal axis is the X-axis.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the vertical axis of a graph called?

options.A: X-axis
options.B: Y-axis
options.C: Z-axis

questions.explanation: The vertical axis is the Y-axis.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Why should the graph scale be checked before reading values?

options.A: A graph may use intervals such as 0, 10, 20 or 0, 50, 100; misreading the interval produces an incorrect value
options.B: The scale always starts at zero
options.C: The scale is only decorative
options.D: The scale shows the title of the graph

questions.explanation: A graph may use intervals such as 0, 10, 20 or 0, 50, 100. Misreading the interval produces an incorrect value.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a truncated axis?

options.A: An axis that starts at a value other than zero, which can visually exaggerate differences
options.B: An axis with no labels
options.C: An axis drawn in a circle
options.D: An axis that shows percentages only

questions.explanation: A truncated axis starts at a value other than zero. It can visually exaggerate differences, so the axis labels and scale must be checked.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a legend or key in a chart?

options.A: It explains the colours, patterns, lines, or symbols used to identify different data series
options.B: It gives the title of the chart
options.C: It shows the unit only

questions.explanation: A legend explains the colours, patterns, lines, or symbols used to identify different data series.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a percentage?

options.A: A quantity expressed as a fraction of 100, represented by the symbol %
options.B: A comparison of two quantities by division
options.C: The sum of all values
options.D: The middle value of a data set

questions.explanation: A percentage expresses a quantity as a fraction of 100 and is represented by the symbol %.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the basic percentage formula?

options.A: Percentage = (Part ÷ Whole) × 100
options.B: Percentage = (Whole ÷ Part) × 100
options.C: Percentage = Part × Whole × 100

questions.explanation: Percentage = (Part ÷ Whole) × 100.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is a part calculated when the percentage and whole are known?

options.A: Part = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Whole
options.B: Part = (Whole ÷ Percentage) × 100
options.C: Part = Percentage × Whole

questions.explanation: Part = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Whole.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is the whole calculated when the part and percentage are known?

options.A: Whole = (Part × 100) ÷ Percentage
options.B: Whole = (Percentage × 100) ÷ Part
options.C: Whole = Part × Percentage

questions.explanation: Whole = (Part × 100) ÷ Percentage.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is percentage increase calculated?

options.A: [(New value − Original value) ÷ Original value] × 100
options.B: [(Original value − New value) ÷ Original value] × 100
options.C: [(New value − Original value) ÷ New value] × 100

questions.explanation: Percentage increase = [(New value − Original value) ÷ Original value] × 100.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is percentage decrease calculated?

options.A: [(Original value − New value) ÷ Original value] × 100
options.B: [(New value − Original value) ÷ Original value] × 100
options.C: [(Original value − New value) ÷ New value] × 100

questions.explanation: Percentage decrease = [(Original value − New value) ÷ Original value] × 100.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does the percentage change formula indicate?

options.A: Percentage change = [(Final value − Initial value) ÷ Initial value] × 100; a positive result indicates an increase and a negative result indicates a decrease
options.B: Percentage change = [(Initial value − Final value) ÷ Final value] × 100; always positive
options.C: Percentage change = Final value + Initial value
options.D: Percentage change = Final value × Initial value

questions.explanation: Percentage change = [(Final value − Initial value) ÷ Initial value] × 100. A positive result indicates an increase and a negative result indicates a decrease.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A value rises from 200 to 250. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explanation: Increase = 50. Percentage increase = (50 ÷ 200) × 100 = 25%.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A value falls from 500 to 400. What is the percentage decrease?
questions.explanation: Decrease = 100. Percentage decrease = (100 ÷ 500) × 100 = 20%.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is 20% of 450?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A class has 240 students and 35% are girls. How many girls are there?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If 72 is 30% of a number, what is the number?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the percentage equivalent of 1/2?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the percentage equivalent of 1/4?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the percentage equivalent of 3/4?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the percentage equivalent of 1/5?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the percentage equivalent of 1/8?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the percentage equivalent of 1/10?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the approximate percentage equivalent of 1/3?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the approximate percentage equivalent of 2/3?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If A is 25% more than B, by what percentage is B less than A?
questions.explanation: If B = 100, A = 125. The difference 25 is 25/125 × 100 = 20% of A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If A is 20% less than B, by what percentage is B more than A?
questions.explanation: If B = 100, A = 80. The difference 20 is 20/80 × 100 = 25% of A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a value increases by 20% and then decreases by 20%, is the final value unchanged?

options.A: Yes, it returns exactly to the original value
options.B: No; taking 100 as the starting value, 100 × 1.20 × 0.80 = 96, giving a net decrease of 4%
options.C: No; the net change is an increase of 4%

questions.explanation: Taking 100 as the starting value: 100 × 1.20 × 0.80 = 96. The net decrease is 4%.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the formula for the net effect of successive percentage changes a% and b%?

options.A: Net percentage change = a + b + (ab ÷ 100), using a negative sign for a decrease
options.B: Net percentage change = a + b
options.C: Net percentage change = a × b ÷ 100

questions.explanation: Net percentage change = a + b + (ab ÷ 100), using a negative sign for a decrease. The result is a percentage increase if positive and decrease if negative.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A value increases by 10% and then by 20%. What is the total percentage increase?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A value decreases by 10% and then by 20%. What is the total percentage decrease?
questions.explanation: Using signed changes: −10 − 20 + [(−10)(−20) ÷ 100] = −30 + 2 = −28. The total decrease is 28%.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a percentage-point difference?

options.A: The arithmetic difference between two percentages, e.g., a rise from 20% to 25% is 5 percentage points
options.B: The relative change compared with the original percentage
options.C: The product of two percentages

questions.explanation: Percentage points measure the direct subtraction of two percentage values. A rise from 20% to 25% is 5 percentage points, while the relative percentage increase is 25%.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between percentage and percentage points?

options.A: Percentage points measure the direct subtraction of two percentage values; percentage change measures the relative change compared with the original percentage
options.B: They are exactly the same thing
options.C: Percentage points are always larger than percentage change
options.D: Percentage change is measured in degrees

questions.explanation: Percentage points measure the direct subtraction of two percentage values; percentage change measures the relative change compared with the original percentage.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a ratio?

options.A: A comparison of two or more quantities of the same kind by division, written using a colon such as 3:5
options.B: A fraction that describes a part of a whole only
options.C: The sum of two quantities

questions.explanation: A ratio compares two or more quantities of the same kind by division and is written using a colon, such as 3:5.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does the ratio 3:5 mean?

options.A: For every 3 parts of the first quantity, there are 5 equal parts of the second quantity
options.B: The first quantity is 3 more than the second
options.C: The total is 3 + 5 = 8 parts always
options.D: The second quantity is 5 less than the first

questions.explanation: For every 3 parts of the first quantity, there are 5 equal parts of the second quantity.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How can a ratio be simplified?

options.A: By dividing every term by the greatest common divisor; e.g., 18:24 simplifies to 3:4
options.B: By adding the same number to every term
options.C: By multiplying only the first term
options.D: By converting it to a percentage

questions.explanation: Divide every term by the greatest common divisor. For example, 18:24 simplifies to 3:4.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is a total divided in a given ratio?

options.A: Add the ratio parts, divide the total by that sum to find one part, and multiply by each ratio term
options.B: Divide the total by each ratio term separately
options.C: Multiply the total by each ratio term
options.D: Subtract the ratio terms from the total

questions.explanation: Add the ratio parts, divide the total by that sum to find one part, and multiply by each ratio term.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Divide 720 in the ratio 5:7. What are the shares?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 12. One part = 720 ÷ 12 = 60. The shares are 5 × 60 = 300 and 7 × 60 = 420.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a proportion?

options.A: A statement that two ratios are equal, such as a:b = c:d
options.B: A comparison of two quantities by division
options.C: A percentage of a whole

questions.explanation: A proportion states that two ratios are equal, such as a:b = c:d.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the cross-multiplication rule for a proportion a:b = c:d?

options.A: ad = bc, provided the denominators are non-zero
options.B: ab = cd
options.C: ac = bd

questions.explanation: If a:b = c:d, then ad = bc, provided the denominators are non-zero.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If 4:7 = x:35, what is x?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the ratio of 40 to 60 in simplest form?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If A:B = 2:3 and B:C = 4:5, what is A:B:C?
questions.explanation: Make B equal: 2:3 becomes 8:12 and 4:5 becomes 12:15. Therefore A:B:C = 8:12:15.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If income and expenditure are in the ratio 5:3 and income is 40,000, what is expenditure?
questions.explanation: 5 parts = 40,000, so 1 part = 8,000. Expenditure = 3 parts = 24,000.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If boys:girls = 7:5 and total students are 480, how many girls are there?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 12; one part = 480 / 12 = 40; girls = 5 × 40 = 200.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between a ratio and a fraction?

options.A: A fraction usually describes a part of a whole; a ratio compares quantities and may compare parts with parts or a part with another quantity
options.B: A ratio is always greater than 1; a fraction is always less than 1
options.C: They are exactly the same in all contexts
options.D: A fraction uses a colon; a ratio uses a slash

questions.explanation: A fraction usually describes a part of a whole. A ratio compares quantities and may compare parts with parts or a part with another quantity. The context determines the interpretation.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Can quantities with different units be directly compared in a ratio?

options.A: Yes, units never matter in ratios
options.B: No; they should first be converted to the same unit before forming the ratio
options.C: Yes, but only if both are whole numbers
options.D: No; ratios can never involve measurements

questions.explanation: They should first be converted to the same unit. For example, convert metres and centimetres to a common unit before forming the ratio.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If A is twice B, what is A:B?
questions.explanation: If A = 2B, then A:B = 2:1.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If A is 40% of B, what is A:B?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Averages, Totals and Basic Comparative Measures
questions.question: What is the arithmetic mean or average?

options.A: Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations
options.B: Average = Number of observations ÷ Sum of observations
options.C: Average = Maximum − Minimum
options.D: Average = Sum of observations × Number of observations

questions.explanation: Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Averages, Totals and Basic Comparative Measures
questions.question: The values are 12, 18, 20, and 30. What is their average?
questions.explanation: Sum = 80; average = 80 ÷ 4 = 20.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Averages, Totals and Basic Comparative Measures
questions.question: If the average of 8 values is 25, what is their total?
questions.explanation: Total = Average × Number = 25 × 8 = 200.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Averages, Totals and Basic Comparative Measures
questions.question: If the average of 5 numbers is 16 and a sixth number 22 is added, what is the new average?
questions.explanation: Original total = 5 × 16 = 80. New total = 80 + 22 = 102. New average = 102 ÷ 6 = 17.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Averages, Totals and Basic Comparative Measures
questions.question: What is a weighted average?

options.A: A simple average where all values have equal importance
options.B: An average that gives different importance or weight to different values, calculated as Sum of (value × weight) ÷ Sum of weights
options.C: The average of only the highest and lowest values
options.D: The median of a data set

questions.explanation: A weighted average gives different importance or weight to different values. Weighted average = Sum of (value × weight) ÷ Sum of weights.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Averages, Totals and Basic Comparative Measures
questions.question: What is the median?

options.A: The most frequently occurring value
options.B: The middle value after arranging observations in ascending or descending order; for an even number, the average of the two middle values
options.C: The difference between maximum and minimum
options.D: The sum of all values divided by the number of values

questions.explanation: The median is the middle value after arranging observations in ascending or descending order. For an even number of observations, it is the average of the two middle values.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Averages, Totals and Basic Comparative Measures
questions.question: What is the mode?

options.A: The middle value of a data set
options.B: The value that occurs most frequently
options.C: The average of all values
options.D: The difference between the largest and smallest values

questions.explanation: The mode is the value that occurs most frequently.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Averages, Totals and Basic Comparative Measures
questions.question: What is the range?

options.A: Maximum value − Minimum value
options.B: Maximum value + Minimum value
options.C: Sum of all values ÷ Number of values

questions.explanation: Range = Maximum value − Minimum value.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Averages, Totals and Basic Comparative Measures
questions.question: What is a total or aggregate?

options.A: The sum of all relevant values in the specified group or period
options.B: The average of all values
options.C: The largest value in a group

questions.explanation: A total or aggregate is the sum of all relevant values in the specified group or period.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Averages, Totals and Basic Comparative Measures
questions.question: What is a per-capita value?

options.A: A quantity multiplied by the population
options.B: A quantity divided by the relevant population, such as per-capita income = total income ÷ population
options.C: The total income of a country
options.D: The average of all income groups

questions.explanation: A per-capita value is a quantity divided by the relevant population, such as per-capita income = total income ÷ population.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Averages, Totals and Basic Comparative Measures
questions.question: What is the growth rate formula?

options.A: [(Current-period value − Previous-period value) ÷ Previous-period value] × 100
options.B: [(Previous-period value − Current-period value) ÷ Current-period value] × 100
options.C: Current-period value ÷ Previous-period value

questions.explanation: Growth rate = [(Current-period value − Previous-period value) ÷ Previous-period value] × 100.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Averages, Totals and Basic Comparative Measures
questions.question: What is the difference between absolute growth and percentage growth?

options.A: Absolute growth is the numerical difference between two values; percentage growth expresses that difference relative to the original value
options.B: Absolute growth is always larger than percentage growth
options.C: Percentage growth is the numerical difference; absolute growth is relative

questions.explanation: Absolute growth is the numerical difference between two values; percentage growth expresses that difference relative to the original value.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is comparative data interpretation?

options.A: It compares two or more categories, groups, locations, or time periods using values, differences, ratios, percentages, averages, or trends
options.B: It only calculates totals
options.C: It only draws pie charts

questions.explanation: Comparative data interpretation compares two or more categories, groups, locations, or time periods using values, differences, ratios, percentages, averages, or trends.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is the absolute difference between two values calculated?

options.A: Absolute difference = Larger value − Smaller value
options.B: Absolute difference = Larger value ÷ Smaller value
options.C: Absolute difference = Larger value + Smaller value
options.D: Absolute difference = Smaller value − Larger value

questions.explanation: Absolute difference = Larger value − Smaller value.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is the percentage by which A exceeds B calculated?

options.A: [(A − B) ÷ B] × 100, assuming B is the reference or base value

questions.explanation: Percentage by which A exceeds B = [(A − B) ÷ B] × 100, assuming B is the reference or base value.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is the percentage by which A is less than B calculated?

options.A: [(B − A) ÷ B] × 100, using B as the base

questions.explanation: Percentage by which A is less than B = [(B − A) ÷ B] × 100, using B as the base.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How do you identify the highest value in a table?

options.A: Compare values in the same unit and for the same measure, then select the largest
options.B: Select the value in the last row
options.C: Select the value in the first column
options.D: Select the most frequently occurring value

questions.explanation: Compare values in the same unit and for the same measure, then select the largest.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How do you identify the lowest value in a chart?

options.A: Read the scale correctly and compare the relevant bars, points, or sectors
options.B: Select the first bar from the left
options.C: Select the bar with the most colour
options.D: Select the value in the title

questions.explanation: Read the scale correctly and compare the relevant bars, points, or sectors.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How do you compare two years of production?

options.A: Calculate the absolute difference and, if asked, divide the difference by the earlier year's value and multiply by 100
options.B: Add the two years' values
options.C: Multiply the two years' values
options.D: Always divide the later year by the earlier year only

questions.explanation: Calculate the absolute difference and, if asked, divide the difference by the earlier year's value and multiply by 100.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How do you compare category shares in a pie chart?

options.A: Compare sector angles or percentages; the larger angle or percentage represents the larger share
options.B: Compare the colours of the sectors
options.C: Count the number of sectors

questions.explanation: Compare sector angles or percentages. The larger angle or percentage represents the larger share.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How do you compare two ratios?

options.A: Convert them to fractions or a common denominator, or cross-multiply to determine which is larger
options.B: Add the terms of each ratio
options.C: Compare only the first terms
options.D: Always select the ratio with larger numbers

questions.explanation: Convert them to fractions or a common denominator, or cross-multiply to determine which is larger.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How do you compare averages of groups with different sizes?

options.A: Calculate each group's total and divide by its own number of observations; do not compare totals as though they were averages
options.B: Compare the totals directly
options.C: Compare the largest value in each group
options.D: Always use the group with more members as the answer

questions.explanation: Calculate each group's total and divide by its own number of observations. Do not compare totals as though they were averages.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a ranking based on data?

options.A: The ordering of categories from highest to lowest or lowest to highest according to a specified measure
options.B: The average of all categories
options.C: The difference between two categories

questions.explanation: A ranking is the ordering of categories from highest to lowest or lowest to highest according to a specified measure.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a trend comparison?

options.A: It compares how values change over several periods, noting increases, decreases, stability, peaks, and troughs
options.B: It compares only two values in one period
options.C: It calculates the average of one period
options.D: It ranks categories in one period only

questions.explanation: A trend comparison compares how values change over several periods, noting increases, decreases, stability, peaks, and troughs.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a base year in comparative analysis?

options.A: A reference year against which values in other years are compared
options.B: The year with the highest value
options.C: The year with the lowest value

questions.explanation: A base year is a reference year against which values in other years are compared.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Why is the base value important in percentage comparison?

options.A: Percentage change depends on the chosen base; the same absolute difference can produce different percentage changes when the base values differ
options.B: The base value is always 100
options.C: The base value does not affect percentage change
options.D: The base value is always the larger number

questions.explanation: Percentage change depends on the chosen base. The same absolute difference can produce different percentage changes when the base values differ.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a total-based DI question?

options.A: It asks for the sum of values across specified categories or periods
options.B: It asks for the difference between two values
options.C: It asks for the average of selected values
options.D: It asks for a ratio between quantities

questions.explanation: A total-based DI question asks for the sum of values across specified categories or periods.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a difference-based DI question?

options.A: It asks how much one value exceeds or falls below another
options.B: It asks for the sum of values
options.C: It asks for the average of values
options.D: It asks for a missing value

questions.explanation: A difference-based DI question asks how much one value exceeds or falls below another.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is an average-based DI question?

options.A: It asks for the mean of selected values or groups
options.B: It asks for the sum of values
options.C: It asks for the largest value

questions.explanation: An average-based DI question asks for the mean of selected values or groups.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a percentage-based DI question?

options.A: It asks for a share, increase, decrease, or percentage comparison using a stated base
options.B: It asks only for totals
options.C: It asks only for differences

questions.explanation: A percentage-based DI question asks for a share, increase, decrease, or percentage comparison using a stated base.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a ratio-based DI question?

options.A: It asks for a comparison between two or more quantities in simplified ratio form
options.B: It asks for the sum of values
options.C: It asks for the average of values
options.D: It asks for a trend over time

questions.explanation: A ratio-based DI question asks for a comparison between two or more quantities in simplified ratio form.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a missing-value DI question?

options.A: It provides partial information and requires an unknown value to be calculated using totals, percentages, ratios, or averages
options.B: It asks only for the highest value
options.C: It asks only for the lowest value
options.D: It asks for a graph to be drawn

questions.explanation: A missing-value DI question provides partial information and requires an unknown value to be calculated using totals, percentages, ratios, or averages.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a trend-based DI question?

options.A: It asks whether a quantity increased, decreased, fluctuated, or remained stable across periods
options.B: It asks for the sum of values
options.C: It asks for a ratio between categories
options.D: It asks for the median only

questions.explanation: A trend-based DI question asks whether a quantity increased, decreased, fluctuated, or remained stable across periods.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a maximum-minimum DI question?

options.A: It asks for the largest or smallest value, difference, share, or growth rate among the categories
options.B: It asks for the average of all categories
options.C: It asks for the total of all categories
options.D: It asks for a missing value

questions.explanation: A maximum-minimum DI question asks for the largest or smallest value, difference, share, or growth rate among the categories.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is an approximate DI question?

options.A: It permits rounded calculations when answer options are sufficiently separated; avoid excessive rounding when options are close
options.B: It always requires exact calculation to two decimal places
options.C: It never allows rounding
options.D: It asks for a graph to be drawn

questions.explanation: An approximate DI question permits rounded calculations when answer options are sufficiently separated. Avoid excessive rounding when options are close.
